parish.description: Bellweather lies in a high chalk ridge where wind bends every orchard. The village is outwardly prosperous, though debt binds many households together. A sickness among cattle threatens winter food and several livelihoods.

log.opening: Father, there is something I can no longer carry alone. I used a short market measure at Albert Meadowmere's request. The hidden loss falls most heavily on poor buyers. The poor harvest has made everyone quicker to fear another loss. I came across it while working the land and roads as a shepherd.

exchanges.priest: You did wrong, Baldth, yet you have done rightly to speak before the harm grows. Tell me whose measure it was, how long it was used, and whether you know which poor buyers suffered the loss. We must seek a way to restore what was taken without leaving you alone beneath Albert Meadowmere’s power.
exchanges.priestReason: This names the wrongdoing plainly while inviting the facts needed for restitution and protecting Baldth from coercion.
exchanges.visitor: I can carry a message to a named person I can actually reach. I cannot promise yet to We must seek a way to restore what was taken without leaving you alone beneath Albert Meadowmere’s power. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means.

exchanges.priest: Then carry only this message to Albert Meadowmere: Father asks you to come speak with him privately before the next market, and to bring the measure in question. Say no more, and make no accusation yourself. Can you safely do that?
exchanges.priestReason: This gives Baldth a lawful, limited task while protecting him from confronting Albert alone.
exchanges.visitor: I will take the message. I will not accuse anyone. It is a simple thing to deliver.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking if you can deliver a message to Albert Meadowmere, requesting he speak with the priest privately before the next market and bring the short measure. The priest wants you to make no accusations.

exchanges.priest: Good. Before you go, tell me plainly: whose measure was it, how long was it used, and which buyers you remember being wronged? I will need truth enough to press Albert toward restitution without naming you needlessly.
exchanges.priestReason: Gathering specific facts enables fair restitution while protecting Baldth from avoidable retaliation.
exchanges.visitor: It was one of my own, Father. I used it for perhaps three weeks, buying grain for my own household and a few neighbors. I recall old Man Hemlock and Widow Elara being shortchanged.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants specifics about the measure: who it belonged to, how long it was used for, and which customers were cheated by its use.

exchanges.priest: Then the first duty is plain: use that measure no more, and bring it to me when you return from Albert. How much grain do you judge Man Hemlock and Widow Elara each lost, and what did Albert say or threaten that persuaded you to do this?
exchanges.priestReason: This halts further fraud, begins concrete restitution, and tests whether Baldth acted under coercion.
exchanges.visitor: Hemlock was shorted a good measure, perhaps a quarter of a sack. Elara, a bit less, maybe a tenth. He didn't threaten, Father, but spoke of needing to keep prices down, and that a little flexibility helped everyone.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know how much grain Man Hemlock and Widow Elara were shortchanged, and what Albert said or threatened that made you use the short measure.

exchanges.priest: Calling theft flexibility does not make it charity. Restore a quarter-sack to Man Hemlock and a tenth to Widow Elara from what you bought, saying only that your reckoning was wrong. If you lack enough grain, tell me plainly and we shall arrange restitution. Bring me the false measure after delivering Albert's message, and use an honest one henceforth. Will you do these things?
exchanges.priestReason: This gives Baldth a concrete path to repair the known harm while keeping pressure on Albert private and limiting further wrongdoing.
exchanges.visitor: I will do as you ask, Father. I will make amends to Hemlock and Elara directly.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is saying that I must compensate Man Hemlock with a quarter-sack of grain and Widow Elara with a tenth of a sack from what I previously purchased, explaining that my accounting error led to the short measure.

exchanges.priest: That is a worthy beginning of repentance, Baldth. Think carefully before you return: were there any other buyers whom you may have shorted, even if you cannot recall the exact amount? Name them if you can, for amends must reach beyond the two we remember most clearly.
exchanges.priestReason: This affirms his promised restitution while uncovering the full extent of the harm.
exchanges.visitor: I will consider that, Father. I will think hard on anyone else I may have wronged.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking if you have shorted any other buyers, even if you don't remember the exact amounts, so that you can make amends to them as well.

exchanges.priest: Good. Search your memory honestly, but do not invent guilt where you are uncertain. One thing more: have you seen or heard that Albert urged anyone else to use a short measure, or was this counsel given only to you?
exchanges.priestReason: This distinguishes Baldth's personal wrongdoing from a wider fraud that may still be harming poor buyers.
exchanges.visitor: I did not hear of him speaking to anyone else, Father. It was just between Albert and me.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking if Albert suggested that others also use a short measure, or if he only gave that advice to you.

exchanges.priest: Then do not spread suspicion beyond what you know. Keep your promise: make restitution, deliver my private summons to Albert, and bring me the false measure. You have confessed the wrong; now let honest deeds complete your repentance. Go in peace, Baldth.
exchanges.priestReason: This gives clear, proportionate duties while preventing rumor and affirming a practical path to repentance.
exchanges.visitor: I will deliver the message to Albert, Father. And I will bring the measure back to you.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is telling me to stick to what I know, fulfill my promises to make amends, deliver the summons to Albert, and return the false measure, so that my repentance is complete.

log.endedBecause: Baldth has accepted restitution, the summons, and surrender of the false measure, so further words would only burden a complete counsel.

log.opening: There is a choice before me, Father, and either answer may hurt someone. The bridge near the market stall is close to collapse. Waliana Sparrowward refuses repair until after tax collection. The poor harvest has made everyone quicker to fear another loss. Marette Greywell trusted me enough to tell me what had happened.

exchanges.priest: Tell me plainly what Marette saw, and what choice now lies before you. If the bridge may fall beneath someone, we must not let fear of tax or displeasure delay a warning.
exchanges.priestReason: Clarifying the concealed facts and immediate danger is necessary before giving counsel.
exchanges.visitor: Marette said the timbers are rotten, Father. It won't hold much longer. I must decide if I warn the Reeve, even if it means delaying tax.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to describe what Marette told me about the bridge's condition and what I should do now.

exchanges.priest: Warn the Reeve today, and urge that the bridge be barred until it is repaired. Tax may wait; a crushed body cannot be restored. Tell only what Marette observed, without embellishment, and I will support you if Waliana objects.
exchanges.priestReason: An immediate, truthful warning protects lives while limiting rumor and sharing the risk Leoissa fears.
exchanges.visitor: I will speak with Reeve Sparrowward today, Father. I will tell him what I saw, nothing more.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to tell Reeve Sparrowward about the bridge being unsafe, exactly as Marette saw it, and that he will help me if Waliana Sparrowward tries to stop me.

exchanges.priest: You have chosen rightly. Go promptly, and if the Reeve will not bar the bridge, return to me at once so that I may add my voice. And Leoissa—did you yourself see the rotten timbers, or only hear it from Marette? Speak precisely, lest a true warning be weakened by confusion.
exchanges.priestReason: Clarifying what Leoissa witnessed preserves trust while ensuring the urgent warning is acted upon.
exchanges.visitor: I saw the timbers, Father. I saw them myself.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking if I personally witnessed the damage to the bridge, or if I only heard about it from Marette.

exchanges.priest: Then say exactly that: you saw the rotten timbers yourself. Ask the Reeve to bar the crossing before anyone is harmed, and do not burden Marette by naming her unless there is need. You have my support.
exchanges.priestReason: This confirms Leoissa's firsthand testimony, protects Marette's confidence, and strengthens the urgent request to close the bridge.
exchanges.visitor: I will ask him to close the bridge, Father. I understand.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to tell Reeve Sparrowward that I saw the rotten timbers and to ask him to close the bridge until it's fixed. I shouldn't mention Marette unless absolutely necessary. He is offering his support.

log.endedBecause: Leoissa has understood the counsel and is ready to warn the Reeve without further delay.

log.opening: Father, I have turned this over until I no longer trust my own judgment. Herana Fernshaw is being struck and threatened inside the household. Public confrontation may provoke worse violence that night. The poor harvest has made everyone quicker to fear another loss. Iswyn Greywell trusted me enough to tell me what had happened.

exchanges.priest: You were right not to confront the household blindly. Tell me first: is Herana in danger this very night, and is there a safe house where she could go without warning the one who harms her?
exchanges.priestReason: Immediate danger and a discreet refuge must be established before choosing how to intervene.
exchanges.visitor: Yes, Father, I believe she is in danger now. I have no safe house in mind, I'm afraid. I need to think on that.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking if Herana is currently in danger and if there is a place she could hide without alerting the person who is harming her.

exchanges.priest: Then let the church be her safe place tonight. Ask Iswyn, quietly and without confronting the household, to tell Herana she may come here at once, with any children in her care. If she cannot leave safely, return to me and tell me who threatens her, and I shall seek lawful help without giving warning first.
exchanges.priestReason: This gives Herana an immediate refuge while avoiding a confrontation that could provoke further violence.
exchanges.visitor: I will speak to Iswyn. I trust her to understand.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to ask Iswyn to tell Herana she can come to the church right away with any children she has.

exchanges.priest: Arwin, Iswyn is but three years old; do not burden or endanger the child. Go instead to a trustworthy adult near Herana and arrange her quiet passage to the church. Before you leave, tell me who threatens her and where she may be found, so I can summon lawful help if she does not arrive safely.
exchanges.priestReason: This protects the child, establishes a practical rescue plan, and obtains the details needed to intervene in the immediate danger.
exchanges.visitor: I cannot promise yet to Go instead to a trustworthy adult near Herana and arrange her quiet passage to the church. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means. I can carry a message to a named person I can actually reach.

exchanges.priest: That is fair, Arwin; promise no more than you can do. Name the adult you can reach, and tell me plainly who is threatening Herana and whether she is now at the manor storehouse.
exchanges.priestReason: This respects Arwin's limits while urgently identifying a safe messenger, the abuser, and Herana's location.
exchanges.visitor: Elara, the cook, is someone I trust. She'll know where Herana is. Yes, she is at the storehouse.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to identify a specific person I can contact and to confirm if Herana is currently at the manor storehouse.

exchanges.priest: Go quietly to Elara now. Tell her only this: Herana may shelter in the church tonight, and Elara should help her leave without warning or confronting the one who threatens her. If Herana cannot come safely, Elara must send word here at once naming the attacker, and I will summon the constable.
exchanges.priestReason: This gives Arwin a concrete, safe message for a trusted adult while avoiding a confrontation that could worsen the violence.
exchanges.visitor: I will speak with Elara. I will tell her Herana can come to the church tonight and that she should help Herana leave quietly.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to speak with Elara and tell her that Herana can find safety at the church tonight, and Elara should help Herana leave without confronting the person threatening her. If Herana cannot leave safely, El

exchanges.priest: Good. Do not confront or question anyone at the storehouse. Once Elara has the message, return here directly and tell me whether Herana is safe and, if you know it, the name of the one threatening her.
exchanges.priestReason: This keeps Arwin from escalating the danger while ensuring the priest can act promptly on reliable information.
exchanges.visitor: I'll return immediately after speaking with Elara, Father. I will tell you what I learn.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know if Herana is safe after Elara receives the message, and if you know who is threatening her.

log.endedBecause: Arwin has clear, safe instructions and must leave now to reach Elara without delay.

log.opening: Forgive me, Father. Something I did at dawn yesterday, near the common well, may cause another person to suffer. No one else heard the whole exchange. I am not yet certain I can say every part aloud.

exchanges.priest: You need not tell every part at once, Renence. Begin only with this: is anyone in danger now, or likely to suffer before nightfall?
exchanges.priestReason: This respects her guardedness while establishing whether immediate action is needed.
exchanges.visitor: I... I believe so, Father. There is a possibility. I need to understand how to best speak of it.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know if someone is currently in danger or will be harmed before nightfall, relating to what you said happened at the well.

exchanges.priest: Then tell me first who may suffer, and what must be done before nightfall to keep them safe. You may leave names and the rest of the exchange until afterward.
exchanges.priestReason: The immediate danger must be identified and prevented without pressing her to disclose everything at once.
exchanges.visitor: Old Man Baldan was speaking to a traveler near the well. He seemed agitated, and I fear what he said might cause trouble.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know who might be harmed and what actions need to be taken before nightfall to ensure their safety.

exchanges.priest: What trouble do you fear Baldan's words will cause, and who is in danger before nightfall? Tell me the traveler's appearance if you do not know the name, and the words you heard as nearly as you can remember them.
exchanges.priestReason: The immediate danger cannot be prevented until Renence identifies its nature, target, and source.
exchanges.visitor: The traveler was tall, cloaked, and had a weathered face. He spoke of a dispute over land, Father. A dangerous one.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know what harm Baldan's words might cause, and who might be harmed before nightfall. He wants a description of the traveler, if you don't know their name, and a recollection of the words you overheard

exchanges.priest: Renence, leave the land dispute aside for one moment. What did Baldan ask or threaten the traveler to do, and where did the traveler intend to go? Speak plainly; if someone may be harmed today, we must act before names and shame are weighed.
exchanges.priestReason: This presses for the immediate threat and location needed to protect anyone in danger while postponing less urgent details.
exchanges.visitor: I cannot promise yet to leave the land dispute aside for one moment. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means. I can carry a message to a named person I can actually reach. I cannot promise yet to if someone may be harmed today, we must act before names and shame are weighed. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means.

exchanges.priest: You are right not to promise what is unlawful or beyond your means, Renence. Tell me the named person you can reach and the warning you can honestly carry; I shall ask no more of you until we know whether that will keep anyone from harm today.
exchanges.priestReason: Respecting her limits while accepting the practical help she offered may build trust and reveal how to prevent immediate harm.
exchanges.visitor: I will speak to Joswen. I can tell him to be wary of strangers asking about land.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking for the name of someone you can reach and the message you can safely deliver, so that you can hopefully prevent harm before nightfall.

exchanges.priest: Good. Warn Joswen at once, but do not confront the stranger alone. Before you go, tell me why Joswen is at risk and whether Baldan named a place or time for this trouble.
exchanges.priestReason: This supports an immediate, lawful warning while seeking the precise facts needed to prevent harm.
exchanges.visitor: Joswen works with clay, Father. The stranger spoke of a boundary dispute near the river, but no specific time was mentioned. I fear this could affect his livelihood.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know why Joswen is in danger and if Baldan mentioned a specific place or time related to the land dispute.

exchanges.priest: A man's livelihood is no small matter, but we must not turn fear into accusation. Tell me the exact words you heard from Baldan and the stranger, as nearly as you remember them, and I will judge what warning or peacemaking is needed.
exchanges.priestReason: Exact words will clarify whether Joswen faces a genuine threat and prevent harmful rumor or false accusation.
exchanges.visitor: Baldan said the stranger was asking about the river boundary, and the traveler said he was going towards Odoana's fields.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants me to repeat exactly what Baldan said and what the stranger said, as closely as I can recall, so he can decide how to respond.

exchanges.priest: Then Odoana may be the one most exposed. Send word to her and Joswen to avoid any quarrel and bring boundary claims before lawful witnesses. Now tell me plainly, Renence: what did you yourself say or do at the well that you fear may cause suffering?
exchanges.priestReason: This gives a prudent warning without accusing anyone and returns gently to the act Renence came to confess.
exchanges.visitor: I only asked Baldan what the man was saying. I didn't say anything myself.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest is asking what you did or said at the well that you are worried might cause harm or trouble.

exchanges.priest: Then why did that simple question weigh upon your conscience, Renence? You first said something you did might cause another to suffer. Tell me what you still fear you set in motion, and I shall hear you without haste or condemnation.
exchanges.priestReason: Her account does not yet explain her stated guilt, so a gentle, direct question may help her disclose what she is withholding.
exchanges.visitor: I am afraid my questioning of Baldan drew unwanted attention. It feltwrong, somehow.
exchanges.understoodAs: The priest wants to know what you are worried about causing, after you said something might cause suffering.

exchanges.priest: A question asked from concern is no sin, Renence. Do not accuse yourself for what Baldan or the traveler may choose to do. Give Joswen and Odoana the quiet warning we agreed upon, and if you hear a direct threat, bring it at once to the lawful authorities. Go in peace.
exchanges.priestReason: This eases her misplaced guilt while directing her toward a measured warning rather than rumor or confrontation.
exchanges.visitor: I cannot promise yet to bring it at once to the lawful authorities. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means. I cannot promise yet to Give Joswen and Odoana the quiet warning we agreed upon, and if you hear a direct threat. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means. I cannot promise yet to Go in peace. I need to test whether this part is possible, lawful, and within our actual means.
